text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Manning wants separation debate: Reform Leader would exclude NDP and Bloc, cites U.S. example on slavery issue.
- Fine catches of cod reported: Reopened fishery deepens division.
- Duceppe minimizes own role in Bloc: Leader's tenure looks fragile.
- Kabila's arrival in Kinshasa fails to clear political waters: Officials issue contradictory statements on election.
- Gustafsen rebels guilty of trespassing: Leader acquitted of attempted murder.
- Minority homosexuals invisible to their world: Gay men and women in Canada's ethnic communities feel surrounded by homophobia, marginalized by gay culture.
- BC Sugar likes Pattison bid: Refiner accepts C$261-million offer for whole company despite higher per-share proposal.
- Fed keeps rates steady: But experts say increase inevitable.
- 'No money made' on scam gold site, Delgratia says: Nasdaq to consider if company shares will continue trading.
- Canada 4th best competitor: Economic forum ranks 53 nations.
- Molson nears Coors deal: Pressure builds for brewer to pay up to C$300 million to buy back stake from Miller or negotiate new licensing deal.
- Pattison bids for all of BC Sugar.
